documented_behavior: android.widget.EditText is an editable text UI element.
android.text.InputType configures input classification; TYPE_CLASS_NUMBER is the class for numeric text, with signed and decimal input represented by additional flags.
android.widget.TextView.getText(), inherited by EditText, returns the displayed editable text.
java.lang.Integer.parseInt(String) parses a signed decimal integer and throws java.lang.NumberFormatException when its String is not a parsable integer.
The documented integer-parser behavior identifies empty input and values not representable as int as NumberFormatException cases; 2147483648 is an out-of-range example.
preconditions: For successful Integer.parseInt(String), the argument must represent a signed base-10 int.
An empty String is not a parsable int.
A decimal representation outside the Java int domain is not a parsable int.
UI input classification must not be treated as proof of the parser's non-empty and bounded-value preconditions.
unknowns: Whether the reported calls use direct getText().toString() values, a helper, a trimmed value, a default value, or another transformation.

security_semantics.runtime_claim: At runtime, NumberFormatException occurs only if a reached Integer.parseInt invocation receives a String that is not a parsable signed decimal int. An application-level crash requires the exception to propagate uncaught through the relevant execution boundary.

name: NumberFormatCrashSpec
semantic_scope: The detector finding is a static candidate concerning a Save-button callback registered from com.mine.autoshine.MainActivity.onCreate. It reports direct parsing of eight EditText-derived values with java.lang.Integer.parseInt and no exception handling evident to the detector. The semantic concern is a feasible uncaught java.lang.NumberFormatException from editable UI text, mapped at the weakness level to CWE-248.
known_false_positive_shapes: The parse is covered by a local, enclosing, delegated, or framework-level handler that the detector does not resolve.
A dominating validation or invariant proves every parsed string is non-empty and within the signed int range on every feasible Save path.
The apparently parsed listener is not the listener attached to the actual Save button, is replaced later, or is unreachable.
The reported EditText values are initialized and made non-editable before the listener can run.
The value reaching Integer.parseInt is transformed by a helper that supplies a safe fallback or rejects invalid input before parsing.
The reported numeric input configuration belongs to a different field, layout variant, flavor, or runtime configuration than the field reaching the parser.
protocol: MainActivity.onCreate → setOnClickListener → user tap → EditText.getText().toString() → Integer.parseInt(...) → NumberFormatException when the value is not a parsable signed decimal int → uncaught propagation if no effective handler exists

detector_examples.message: Static candidate (not executed): the Save button listener registered in onCreate calls Integer.parseInt on eight EditText values with no exception handling; the fields use inputType=number, which still allows an empty field and values beyond Integer.MAX_VALUE, so clearing one field and tapping Save throws NumberFormatException and crashes the app (CWE-248).
